title: Stretches for tight hips and pain from sitting too long
intro: Sitting for long hours at the office or in the car can make your hips feel tight and stiff. A few gentle stretches every day can help your hips feel more comfortable and move more easily.
muscles: Front of the hips (hip flexors), glutes, hamstrings and outer hips. These stretches are for comfort and movement, not for reducing fat on your hips or thighs.
steps: Seated figure-4 stretch: sit on a chair, place your right ankle on your left knee, lean forward slightly with your back straight.
Standing hip flexor stretch: stand, step one leg back, squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward slightly, hands on the wall.
Seated hamstring stretch: sit at the edge of a chair, straighten one leg, heel on the floor, lean forward from your hips.
Seated twist: sit upright, slowly twist your body to the right and left, hands on the chair backrest.
Hold each stretch for 20-30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Bouncing during the stretch. Hold it calmly.
Stretching until it hurts. You should only feel a mild pull, not pain.
Rounding your back when leaning forward. Bend from your hips and keep your back straight.
easier: Reduce the range, for example lean only a little, or hold for 10-15 seconds. All stretches can be done seated or while holding onto a wall.
harder: Hold for up to 45 seconds, or add a kneeling hip flexor stretch with a cushion under your knee if your knee is comfortable. Avoid positions that cause knee or back pain.
dose: 2-3 times per stretch, hold 20-30 seconds. Do it every day, 5-10 minutes. It is also good to get up and move for 2-3 minutes every 30-60 minutes of sitting.
safety: Stop if there is sharp pain, numbness, or an electric-shock feeling running down your leg. If hip or back pain keeps going, gets worse, or comes after a fall, see a doctor or physio.

faq.q: Can I do these stretches at the office?
faq.a: Yes. The figure-4, hamstring and twist stretches can all be done on an office chair. Take 5 minutes during your break or before going home.

faq.q: Why are my hips tight even though I don't exercise?
faq.a: Sitting for long periods keeps the muscles at the front of your hips in a shortened position for a long time. When you stand up, they feel tight. Mixing sitting with short bouts of standing and walking can help.

faq.q: Can these stretches make my hips and thighs smaller?
faq.a: No, and no exercise can remove fat from just one spot. Fat goes down overall through eating and movement. These stretches help your body feel more comfortable and move more easily.
